Note::TexAccessor::to_markdown¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signatures¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::to_markdown() const
Note Note::TexAccessor::to_markdown(std::int64_t mode) const

Convert A Recognized TeX Subset To Markdown¶

to_markdown() rewrites a fixed set of common TeX commands to their Markdown equivalents — headings, bold, italic/emphasis, and list items — and removes color wrappers, hyperlink commands, labels, references, citations, packages, bibliography commands, spacing/delimiter commands, and font commands. Use it for a quick, best-effort Markdown preview of simple TeX prose; it is not a full document converter.

The recognized rewrites, applied in this order:

TeX

Markdown

\section{...} / \section*{...}

\n# ...\n

\subsection{...} / \subsection*{...}

\n## ...\n

\subsubsection{...} / \subsubsection*{...}

\n### ...\n

\textbf{...}

**...**

\emph{...} / \textit{...}

*...*

\item

-

to_markdown() and to_html both remove \textcolor/ \colorbox wrappers (keeping their content) and unwrap \href/hyperref commands (keeping the visible label) — the two converters agree on that point. They still differ on one rewrite: to_html maps a TeX linebreak (\\) to <br/>, but to_markdown has no rewrite for it and leaves it as a literal \\ in the output.

mode¶

mode = 0 (the default) applies the rewrite table and removals above with no further change. mode >= 1 additionally case-folds the resulting Markdown (ASCII lowercase) — the same contract as to_text’s own mode — folding after every rewrite has already run, so Markdown punctuation such as # and * is unaffected (it has no case) while headings and prose text fold. Negative values behave like 0. to_html has no mode parameter at all.

The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. Undefined input remains undefined; Bool, Int64, Float64, and Bytes receivers are rejected because TeX source is Text.

Example 1: Headings, Inline Formatting, Item, Color, And A Link¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({
    R"(\section{Intro}\subsection{Detail}\subsubsection{Fine})",
    R"(\textbf{Bold} and \emph{emphasis} \item first)",
    R"(\textcolor{red}{warn} \href{https://example.test}{link} \label{x} \ref{x}.)"})
    .tex().to_markdown()
    << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["# Intro ## Detail ### Fine", "**Bold** and *emphasis* - first", "warn link ."]

The third cell shows both removals: \textcolor{red}{warn} becomes bare warn, and \href{...}{link} becomes bare link — both unwrapped rather than passed through — while \label{x} and \ref{x} are removed entirely. to_html treats this exact cell identically.

Example 2: mode >= 1 Case-Folds¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\section{Intro}\subsection{Detail}\subsubsection{Fine})",
    R"(\textbf{Bold} and \emph{emphasis} \item first)",
    R"(\textcolor{red}{warn} \href{https://example.test}{link} \label{x} \ref{x}.)"});
std::cout << source.tex().to_markdown(1) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["# intro ## detail ### fine", "**bold** and *emphasis* - first", "warn link ."]

Every letter folds to lowercase; the Markdown punctuation #, **, and - is unchanged since punctuation has no case.

Example 3: A 2-D Grid, Shape Preserved¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(\section{A})", R"(\textbf{B})", "plain", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << grid.tex().to_markdown() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["# A", "**B**"], 
  ["plain", ""]
]

Example 4: Undefined And Non-Text Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().to_markdown().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).tex().to_markdown();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "to markdown Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
to markdown Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • to_html: the equivalent conversion to HTML, which shares the same color/hyperlink removal but has no mode parameter and maps a TeX linebreak to <br/> instead of leaving it literal.

  • to_text: drop TeX structure entirely instead of converting it to another markup language.

  • render: a readable Unicode projection instead of markup.
